title: Plural adjective agreement in partitive
summary: Match an adjective to a plural partitive noun inside a phrase.
objectives: Match an adjective to a plural partitive noun inside a phrase.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Match an adjective to a plural partitive noun inside a phrase.
The noun form is provided and the adjective must agree with it. Complete plural adjective alternatives are supplied, including forms with changing stems.
This lesson concerns an adjective before a noun. It does not teach the full rules for plural descriptions after the verb be.
keyPoints: An adjective directly describing this plural partitive noun also takes plural partitive. Match case and number, not just the last letter.

examples.english: I am looking for big cars.
steps: An adjective directly describing this plural partitive noun also takes plural partitive. Match case and number, not just the last letter.
Etsin means “I am looking for” and works as the verb. etsin comes from etsiä: etsi- + -n.
isoja means “big” and works as the plural partitive adjective agreeing with the following noun. Keep iso and add -ja: iso + ja = isoja.
autoja means “cars” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep auto and add -ja: auto + ja = autoja.

examples.english: I am looking for small books.
steps: An adjective directly describing this plural partitive noun also takes plural partitive. Match case and number, not just the last letter.
Etsin means “I am looking for” and works as the verb. etsin comes from etsiä: etsi- + -n.
pieniä means “small” and works as the plural partitive adjective agreeing with the following noun. Use pien- + plural i + -ä = pieniä.
kirjoja means “books” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Replace final a with o, then add -ja: kirjo- + -ja = kirjoja.

examples.english: I am looking for new buses.
steps: An adjective directly describing this plural partitive noun also takes plural partitive. Match case and number, not just the last letter.
Etsin means “I am looking for” and works as the verb. etsin comes from etsiä: etsi- + -n.
uusia means “new” and works as the plural partitive adjective agreeing with the following noun. Use uus- + plural i + -a = uusia.
busseja means “buses” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Change final i to e, then add -ja: busse- + -ja = busseja.

examples.english: I am looking for good toys.
steps: An adjective directly describing this plural partitive noun also takes plural partitive. Match case and number, not just the last letter.
Etsin means “I am looking for” and works as the verb. etsin comes from etsiä: etsi- + -n.
hyviä means “good” and works as the plural partitive adjective agreeing with the following noun. Replace final ä with plural i, then add -ä: hyv-i-ä = hyviä.
leluja means “toys” and works as the plural partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep lelu and add -ja: lelu + ja = leluja.

commonMistakes: Do not use a singular adjective beside the plural partitive noun.
A nominative plural adjective is a different case.
